findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

A food handler was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted to correct. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Cardboard cases of cereal packages was observed on the floor in the dry storage room. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the cases picked up onto shelves to correct. Ensure that all foods and food contact containers are stored off of the floor to prevent possible contamination concerns.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. 

The facility had a lactic acid based sanitizer available for use and only quat based test strips in the facility. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to have test strips that match their sanitizer prior to the scheduled follow-up. Ensure that all food contact chemical concentrations can be verified as correct at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the person in charge (PIC) wash their hands prior to donning gloves, but failed to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was conducted and the PIC was reminded to use a barrier to complete proper hand washing. Ensure a barrier is used at the end of hand washing to prevent re-contaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One Food handler’s license was observed to have expired last month. The PIC stated the employee was on staff today, and that the individual will complete their food handler’s course through a preferred service, paid for by the facility. Ensure all food handler’s maintain their food handler’s license by retaking the course every three years.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was on the premises during today’s inspection. A CFPM is required to be present during all times food is being prepared or served. Inspector suggests an additional food handler obtains their CFPM so that there is a CFPM on site at all times. The presence of a CFPM ensures safe food handling and decreases the incidence of improper food handling and the risk of food-borne illness.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- No paper towels were available at the kitchen hand-sink upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- Upon request, paper towels were provided at the kitchen handwashing sink. Ensure warm running water, soap, and paper towels are always available at handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There is a 2 basin sink in the kitchen area. When the inspector asked the food handler where they wash their hands they stated in the restroom. The restroom is set to close, and therefore poses a risk of contamination freshly cleaned hands. The kitchen sink is used for hand washing and cleaning employee dishes CORRECTED- Inspector spoke with the person in charge (PIC), who will educate employees that handwashing before food prep or service should take place in the right basin of the kitchen sink. Teacher dishes were moved from the right basin to the left basin. Hand washing sinks are designated for hand washing only.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sink in the men’s restroom to be out of soap. CORRECTED- the PIC was notified and the soap was refilled. Ensure all handwashing sinks are always stocked with warm running water, soap, and paper towels (or another means to dry hands).
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: No paper towels were available at the kitchen handsink upon inspector’s arrival. Employees recognized the lack of paper towels and retrieved towels from another location to dry hands, but did not replace the paper towels at the handsink. CORRECTED- Upon request, paper towels were provided at the kitchen handwashing sink. Ensure towels are always available at handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The kitchen dish machine was found to reach a plate temperature of 143F after two cycles. On the second cycle, the dish machine began leaking suds. PIC called to request maintenance on the machine to fix the leak and adjust the rinse temperature. Ensure the rinse temperature is sufficient to reach 180F from the baffle or achieve a surface temperature of 160F, as measured on an irreversible registering temperature indicator.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Facility does not have a way to verify that the dish machine is reaching sanitizing temperature. Ensure that an irreversible, maximum registering thermometer or heat-sensitive stickers are available to monitor the dish machine function.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a way to verify that the dish machine is reaching sanitizing temperature. Ensure an irreversible, maximum registering thermometer or heat-sensitive stickers are available to monitor dish machine function. CORRECTED- PIC ordered heat-sensing strips during this visit.
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Drywall is cut away from the plumbing under the sink in the kitchen. Patch drywall so the wall is closed. Ensure the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]
